name: Dan Schulman

career.title: Sales assistant rising to President of the Consumer Markets Division (18 years)
Independent Lead Director, then Chief Executive Officer

background_rationale: Began in sales at AT&T and spent 18 years in its consumer businesses before leading consumer-facing companies Priceline, Virgin Mobile USA and PayPal.

notable.summary: Verizon began cutting more than 13,000 jobs, about 20% of its non-union management workforce, and set up a $20 million Reskilling and Career Transition Fund for affected employees.
Verizon completed its roughly $20 billion acquisition of Frontier Communications, expanding its fiber footprint to nearly 30 million passings across 31 states and Washington, D.C.
On his first earnings call as CEO, Schulman said "We let our customers down" in reference to a network outage and said Verizon would use AI to optimize operations and reshape the customer experience.
Schulman said AI would cause disruption in certain job functions and that AI agents were handling routine customer-service tasks, with more complex cases handled by agents and humans together.

personal_story.hook: Dan Schulman started at AT&T in the lowest sales job in the Bell system; 45 years later he runs Verizon.
personal_story.summary: Schulman grew up in Princeton, New Jersey, and has said he was born with social activism in his DNA, citing a grandfather who organized unions and his mother's activism. After graduating from Middlebury in 1980 he joined the Bell system as a sales assistant, earning $208.31 every two weeks. In 1986, while a district manager, he lost his 19-year-old sister to a brain aneurysm and stepped away from work for months; he has said that when he returned he stopped taking credit and started giving it to his team, and his rise accelerated. He went on to run AT&T's consumer business, Priceline, Virgin Mobile USA and PayPal, then joined Verizon's board in 2018 and was named its CEO in October 2025.

quote.text: It was a straight line up after that because now I was known as someone that wasn't going to take credit for what you do, I'll give you the credit.
quote.context: Interview with The Berkshire Eagle, Sept. 2019, describing how he changed after his sister's death
